findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition shadows width/height overload
findings.body: The file defines `self.downsize` twice in a row: once as `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and again as `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. In Ruby the second definition overwrites the first, so any existing caller using the 4-argument max_width/max_height form will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments). One overload must be renamed or removed and callers updated.

findings.title: In-place downsize overwrites source and ignores failure
findings.body: The retry loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` using the same path for source and destination and discards the boolean return value. If `convert`/`gifsicle` fails or is killed mid-write, the original upload is corrupted/truncated, and the loop will pointlessly retry the same failing conversion up to 5 times. Use a separate temp destination and only replace on success, and break on failure.

findings.title: Nil tempfile dereferenced after failed download
findings.body: When the API `url` path is used, `FileHelper.download(...) rescue nil` can leave `tempfile` as nil. The new guard correctly checks `if tempfile && ...` but line 72 unconditionally calls `tempfile.size` in `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)`. A failed/oversize download therefore raises NoMethodError on nil instead of returning a clean upload error.

findings.title: Animation detection never matches tempfiles so GIFs are flattened
findings.body: Downsizing passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`, but `OptimizedImage.optimize` decides animation via `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` on the filesystem path. `tempfile.path` (Rack multipart / FileHelper download) does not carry the original `.gif` extension, so the check is false and `downsize_instructions` with `from[0]` is used, stripping animation even when animations are allowed. The check should use `filename`, not the temp path.

findings.title: Client max upload size hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: Both `validateUploadedFile` and the 413 handler previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb']` / `max_image_size_kb`. They now hardcode `10 * 1024`. This breaks per-type limits (attachments vs images), breaks admins who configured a smaller or larger `max_image_size_kb`, and diverges from the server which still validates against the setting, so users get client approval followed by server 422 rejections or vice versa.
